narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 65.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—failure was more likely than passing in its assessment. The strongest factor was your third-year class rank: you were in the second decile, while admitted students averaged around the sixth decile. That low rank pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your first-year rank was the third most influential factor; at the third decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, it also pushed toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score. Your score of 34 is below the accepted-student average of about 37, but in this prediction it actually worked in your favor, pushing toward passing rather than failing. Family income and full-time status were not among the main reasons. To improve a future application, focus on raising your academic performance, especially upper-year class rank, and seek academic support and bar-exam preparation. You should also ask admissions whether updated grades, a supplemental explanation, or evidence of improvement could be considered before you reapply.
